title: The age of agents
description: Forget AGI and chatbots; we’ve officially entered the age of agents. Far beyond standard LLMs, AI agents are embedding into everyday apps to independently solve real-life problems and handle complex tasks. Join Manus AI Co-founder and CPO Tao Zhang - who pioneered agents - to explore why the shift to autonomous agents matters more than the latest foundation model, how it will change daily life for billions, and why the race to control the agent interface is the battle to become tech's next dominant giant.

title: When AI builds itself
description: AI will transform every industry, but none more than AI research itself. Join Recursive & You.com co-founder & CEO Richard Socher as he breaks down how self-improving systems are accelerating their own development and laying the foundation for superintelligence.

title: Back-end developer meetup
description: Back-end developers, this one is for you! Connect with fellow back-end engineers and software architects to discuss microservices, database optimization, API design or whatever else is on your mind.

title: Free or controlled internet? The great DSA debate
description: In December 2020, European Commission President Ursula Von Der Leyen announced the Digital Services Act (DSA) at Web Summit. In an effort to combat so-called hate speech and online misinformation, the legislation has become a crucial part of how European regulators address harms caused by online platforms. However, some free expression advocates have warned of threats to free speech under the guise of tackling incitement. Our panel asks: Is the DSA necessary to combat big tech or an effort to control online discourse?

title: AI-driven R&D: Unlocking precision medicine at scale
description: AI in healthcare is everywhere – but separating genuine breakthroughs from marketing hype is harder than ever. Sanofi CDO Emmanuel Frenehard and Owkin CEO Thomas Clozel cut through the noise with hard-won lessons from the pharma R&D frontlines, discussing why healthcare is both the hardest and most important AI frontier, and how AI agents are reshaping R&D workflows and advancing precision medicine.

title: In the age of AI, trust Is still human
description: Drawing on new research with 700 founders and a decade of building Enfuce, Denise Johansson explores why trust doesn’t slow growth down, it enables it, and why human trust may become even more important as technology and relationships become increasingly automated.

title: The open-source advantage
description: While closed-source frontier models dominate headlines, open-source AI is quietly becoming the default engine for real-world business. This session explores how open models give builders full control over their data, cut compute costs, and speed up innovation. Move past the hype to discover why the future of AI is fast, flexible, and open source.

title: How AI actors are creating entertainment's next frontier
description: Are AI actors a threat to human performance, or the arrival of a new art form? AI actress Tilly Norwood and her creator Eline van der Velden present a bold vision for the future of film and TV. In this session we ask how synthetic performers can sit harmoniously alongside traditional entertainment as a separate, thriving industry built for the next generation of digital-native audiences.

title: The future of Europe: Can it stand on its own feet?
description: For decades, Europe has depended on the US not only for its security, but also for much of its technological and financial infrastructure. As the transatlantic relationship continues to fracture, Europe faces a question much bigger than how to spend more on defence. Can it reduce its dependence on American technology, capital and financial infrastructure while building the industrial capacity to defend itself? And can it do so without sacrificing prosperity and the welfare state?

description: Your AI pilot worked. Now what? Learn a practical framework to overcome cost, integration, and deployment complexity. Discover how to assemble edge architectures that deliver actual business impact. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: Rethinking venture capital
description: As market cycles tighten and exits get longer, standard financial backing isn't enough to help startups succeed. Modern venture capital requires a complete support structure to lower risk and speed up growth. This session focuses on what it takes to turn complex ideas into durable, market-ready companies.

title: The chaos and the campaign
description: Journalism is facing unprecedented disruption, driving audiences toward two extremes: raw, unfiltered frontline reporting on one end, and calm, behind-the-scenes legal and political analysis on the other. This session explores what's driving this divide between the streets and the strategists, whether social media is to blame, and if this surge of content can inspire real-world change.

title: Simulating reality, not just rendering frame rate
description: The next frontier of AI isn't making Hollywood clips – it's building interactive, real-time simulations of the physical world. Join Runway CTO Kamil Sindi as he outlines the rise of General World Models and shows how moving beyond static 2D frames to dynamic, cause-and-effect environments unlocks the future of spatial computing, robotics, and interactive media.

title: Machine-ready brands: A playbook for the Intelligence Age
description: Customers are getting used to agents doing the browsing, deciding, even the buying on their behalf. Once someone's used to that, a static ad or a fixed website starts to feel broken. They expect brands to meet them with the same fluency: responsive, individualized, always-on. This talk is a practical playbook for making that shift: what it takes to define a brand for both humans and machines, and build the systems that keep it consistent, current, and everywhere your customers now expect to find it.

title: Your AI agent just got a passport
description: AI agents are rapidly moving from experiments to the real world. But an agent that works brilliantly in one market won't necessarily work everywhere and language is only the beginning. Culture, context, local expectations and even the way people express intent can change from one place to another. RWS CEO Benjamin Faes explores what businesses need to think about as they build AI agents for a world that's far more complicated than their training data.

title: Chat Control 2.0: the government in your DMs?
description: As Europe debates new measures to combat child sexual abuse online, where should the line be drawn between protecting children and protecting private communications? This talk explores the implications for privacy, encryption, and digital freedom, and whether “private” messages could soon mean something very different.

title: The battery is the new barrel
description: The next energy crisis won't be decided by who has the most oil in the ground, it'll be decided by who has the most energy storage available. This session explores how EV charging and home batteries are quietly becoming one of the most strategic assets in the fight for energy security.

title: Newsfluencers
description: From TikTok to the Times, traditional media is turning to creators to rebuild relationships with audiences who have turned away. In a bid to stay relevant, legacy outlets are enlisting creator clout to stay in the conversation. But does this represent a genuine, long-term partnership – or is it merely a temporary fix while traditional media tries to catch up.

timeslot_participations.name: Vitus Spehar
timeslot_participations.job_title: Creator of Under The Desk News

title: What makes a startup fundable in 2026?
description: Raising capital is no longer about having the great idea, the newest technology, or the most polished pitch. Investors want companies that can keep growing as the market and competition change. In this session, Igor shares how founders should think about building and making decisions if they want to build companies that keep growing in three years from now.

title: Live Podcast: The Big Technology Podcast with Atlassian
description: If Software Was Dead, Why Are We Sitting Here? AI agents were supposed to destroy software companies, But so far, that prediction looks premature or wrong. Atlassian co-founder Mike Cannon-Brookes joins Big Technology’s Alex Kantrowitz to examine why SaaS has held up and what happens as agents start operating software on our behalf. In this talk, they’ll explore whether organisational context (not necessarily model intelligence) is becoming the key advantage in enterprise AI, whether the traditional software interface survives, and where, if at all, the “Saaspocalypse” worries had merit.

title: From 'For You' to 'For Me': The new path from discovery to action
description: On TikTok, people watch it, love it, want it – and increasingly, those moments happen almost all at once. What starts as entertainment can spark curiosity, inspire a search, shape a decision and drive action, reshaping the traditional path from awareness to purchase. TikTok's Global Head of Business Marketing, Isobel Sita-Lumsden, explores how this new era of discovery is changing marketing, from the growing influence of creators and communities to the role of AI in creativity, and how brands can turn cultural relevance into real business growth.

title: Is it time to unify the global payment stack?
description: As global commerce expands and payment ecosystems fragment across regional rails, alternative methods, and legacy architectures, managing transactions efficiently has become a primary bottleneck for enterprise growth. This panel gathers payments leaders and fintech innovators to explore how unified payment infrastructure and smart orchestration layers are reshaping transaction strategy.

title: Who pays for AI and who owns it?
description: Nineteen out of every twenty dollars spent on AI compute buys hardware that sits idle. Drawing on production data from thousands of global deployments, Laurent Gil breaks down the broken economics of AI infrastructure and presents a framework to measure actual ROI and data sovereignty.

title: Has Europe’s tech moment arrived?
description: Europe has an ambition to become a global tech powerhouse, whilst also setting the rules for the digital economy. Can Europe build a technology ecosystem that competes with the US and China while establishing the right governance approach through its rules? In this talk the EU Commission's EVP Henna Virkkunen discusses the EU’s drive for tech sovereignty, from AI and cloud to chips and digital infrastructure, alongside its efforts to regulate the platforms and AI systems reshaping society.

title: Europe in a multipolar world: Rethinking the relationship with BRICS
description: As the BRICS expand their economic, political, and technological influence, Europe faces a fundamental question. How should it navigate a world where power is increasingly dispersed beyond the traditional Western order? This conversation explores Europe’s evolving relationship with China, Brazil and the wider BRICS grouping, and whether Europe can forge a more independent and constructive role in the emerging multipolar order.

title: The next battleground in AI – and it's not the models
description: The AI era is shifting from copilots to agents that can research, reason, decide and act, bringing unprecedented opportunities for enterprise automation, but also unprecedented risk. As autonomy increases, so does the impact of unreliable information. Hallucinations can compound across multiple steps of an agentic workflow, turning a small data error into a major business failure. Statista CEO Marc Berg explores why trusted data, not smarter models, is becoming the critical infrastructure for agentic AI.

title: The AI race is an energy race
description: Every leap in AI, from bigger models to new data centres, runs on electricity, and the demand is higher than most grids were built to handle. This session asks the question shaping the next decade of computing: is this appetite for energy something we can satisfy, or will power become the real limit on how far AI can go?

title: Building the pan-European bank: Scale, governance and European growth
description: As Europe debates its global competitiveness, Revolut is achieving what few tech companies have managed: building a cross-border financial institution at scale. Following the grant of its full French banking licence, Revolut is launching a second EU banking hub to serve more than 30 million customers across western Europe. In this session, Béatrice Cossa-Dumurgier, CEO of western Europe at Revolut, draws on her career across traditional banking, high-level government finance, and scaleup tech to explore what it takes to build a modern, unified European bank – navigating fragmented policy landscapes, combining global technology with local banking infrastructure, and competing against legacy institutions built for a bygone era.

title: Is the future of venture in software or hardware?
description: Is AI's trillion-dollar future built on silicon or written in code? Right now, chipmakers and data centres are capturing record revenues. But as compute scales, will application software, dev tools, and agents claim the long-term margins? Join this session as we debate where sustainable moat, and venture returns will actually settle across the AI stack.

title: The orchestration gap: Fixing the enterprise’s AI problem
description: Companies have invested heavily in AI, but many still struggle to turn it into business impact. A WSJ Intelligence survey of 800 C-suite leaders found that 85% say their tech stacks are disconnected, with little agreement on who should fix them. Dan Gardner explores why orchestration has become the next competitive advantage, and what it takes to connect systems, teams and AI to transform how work gets done.

title: Heads up: AI wearables enter the workplace
description: Smartphones pulled us into our screens. The next generation of AI wearables promises to pull us back out. Will Wang, founder and CEO of Even Realities, looks at how smartglasses are moving from consumer novelty to an everyday work tool. He'll also discuss what developers, employers and workers need to get right in design, privacy and trust before that happens. Plus, an announcement on where technology goes next. If the best interface is the one you barely notice, are we ready to wear it all day?

title: AI: your new news editor?
description: AI agents could become the next major editors of news, searching, gathering and processing information on behalf of people. What does this mean for media organisations and the way news is created, distributed and monetised? This session explores how media companies can prepare for an agent-driven future.

title: Get on bored: Reclaiming our attention span in the workplace
description: As AI automates routine tasks, why are knowledge workers more exhausted than ever? The answer lies in a cultural allergy to boredom and technology’s relentless fight for our focus. This session challenges the myth of continuous optimisation, showing leaders how to design tools and working hour structures that give employees the mental space needed for breakthroughs.

title: The women unmasking digital crime scenes
description: The internet isn’t safe or regulated – and now, it has also become a crime scene. A dangerous digital underworld is emerging as hidden groups on Telegram and public porn websites host international rape networks. As these networks expand globally, more and more women are being harmed. This panel brings together the journalists who exposed these covert networks hiding in plain sight.

title: AI and humans: Building the AI-native organisation
description: Orchestrating complex AI workflows, maintaining human-in-the-loop oversight and scaling operations without exponentially growing headcount is the defining challenge of the AI era. Base44 CPO Yoav Orlev deconstructs how to scale using autonomous AI agents as a primary workforce, offering concrete rules to help build and grow a lean, highly profitable AI-native enterprise.

title: Dogfooding AI security: Lessons from our own SOC [Hosted by Elastic]
description:
Elastic's SOC shares lessons on deploying AI securely: what to automate, when humans must stay involved, and how governance evolves in high-stakes environments.
Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: Everything you need to know about M&A in 2026
description: Navigating tech M&A in 2026 demands more than capital. It requires a playbook built for scale, integration, and sustainable value creation. Join Taxfix CFO Mohamed Omaizat as he breaks down the realities of 2026 dealmaking, from executing multi-market consolidation strategies to evaluating AI-driven targets. Gain practical insights from a veteran finance leader on how to identify acquisition targets, manage regulatory hurdles, and extract true post-merger value in today’s evolving market.

title: Can you trust what you see anymore?
description: AI has made it easier than ever to create content - text, video, and audio. But much of what it creates has very little relationship with reality. In a world flooded with slop, how can trust what we watch, read, and hear?

title: Deep tech in the deep sea
description: We’ve mapped more of Mars than our own ocean floor, leaving 70% of the seabed in total darkness. Now, AI, robotics, and digital twins are lighting up the abyss to power the next wave of global innovation.

title: Title: Bet on the foundation, not the framework
description:
Most conversations about AI independence focus on the model: who trains it, who owns the weights, where inference runs. Samar Abbas, co-founder and CEO of Temporal, will argue that's the wrong place to look. The layer that matters is underneath: the execution infrastructure that decides whether a company can actually change course later.
Frameworks and agent harnesses are cycling through versions faster than almost anything else in tech. Whatever framework looks essential this year will likely be replaced next year. Samar's argument: building capable AI agents means building on an open foundation that outlasts the model, framework, or harness sitting on top of it, and that no single vendor can take away.
Drawing on Temporal's work running durable execution under some of today's most demanding AI workloads, he'll make the case that the real question isn't which model you pick, but whether your infrastructure survives whatever comes next.

title: Sensing the future: Using AI to unlock the next generation of molecular science.
description: What happens when AI moves beyond digital interfaces to interact with the physical and chemical world? From digitising scent and mapping molecular behaviour to creating sustainable food systems, molecular AI turns raw data into real-world sensory intelligence. Bringing together computational biology, sensory technology and culinary innovation, this session demonstrates how AI-driven science is opening up multibillion-dollar opportunities across health, consumer products and global food infrastructure.

title: AI’s holy grail: From uncertain systems to reliable outcomes
description: The biggest challenge in enterprise AI is execution that yields guaranteed outcomes at scale: turning rapidly evolving capabilities into systems that reliably deliver value. Toptal CEO Taso Du Val examines a framework for engineering deterministic outcomes from inherently nondeterministic AI by bringing together highly specialized systems, frontier-level expertise and guardrails to make AI reliable at enterprise scale.

title: The agentic internet: Who controls the web?
description: AI agents are changing how people discover information, shop, and transact online. As more activity happens without a human click, the web is facing new questions about control, attribution, and value. Cloudflare co-founder and CEO Matthew Prince explains why the internet is at a turning point - what this shift means for companies of every size and what it will take to keep the web open in the agentic era.

title: The sovereign creator
description: Social platforms leave creators at the mercy of sudden algorithm changes and heavy revenue cuts. beehiiv Co-Founder and CEO Tyler Denk outlines the shift to direct audience ownership and shows how creators can take back control, leveraging social platforms for growth while converting followers into owned-and-operated media businesses.

title: Regulation is killing European fintech
description: European regulation is simultaneously the best and worst thing about building fintech here. It protects consumers, but it also protects incumbents, raises the cost of experimentation and arguably explains a big chunk of why Europe keeps falling behind the U.S. and Asia in producing category-defining companies. In this conversation we're exploring how regulation in Europe is death by a thousand rules.

title: Postmodern warfare: How cheap technology is disrupting the battlefield
description: Modern warfare is being reshaped by a striking asymmetry: cheap drones, software and off-the-shelf technology can now challenge weapons costing millions or even billions. Has the advantage shifted from expensive, sophisticated platforms to low-cost, adaptable and scalable systems? And what does this mean for the future of defence, deterrence and geopolitics?

title: Beyond scale: Why the future of AI is efficient
description: AI has grown by getting bigger: more data, more compute, larger clusters. The next leap is about getting smarter per parameter. ModelBest co-founder and CEO Dahai Li explains how high-density foundation models break the limits of massive infrastructure - out of the cloud and onto everyday devices, making it affordable, private, responsive. Does the future of AI belong to brute-force scale, or intelligent efficiency?

title: Fusion's fork in the road
description: No fusion power plant has ever produced more energy than it consumes, yet the race to commercialise it is already splitting in two. One path bets everything on building the full-scale power plant first; the other funds itself by selling what fusion can already do today, like medical isotopes, one step at a time. The question is which bet pays off first.

title: Who’s steering the machine? Keeping people at the centre of the future workforce
description: As artificial intelligence rapidly transforms the modern enterprise, long term organisational success still hinges on prioritising human potential, culture, and purpose. In this fireside chat, Lattice CEO Sarah Franklin explores why leaders must keep humanity at the helm, demonstrating how a people-first approach drives elite performance and meaningful growth in an AI driven world.

title: Leading accessibility in the AI era: New challenges, new opportunities
description: AI is accelerating how digital products are built, while accessibility requirements are evolving across markets. For companies, that creates a new set of questions: how do you build accessibility into increasingly AI-driven products, how should organisations respond to changing requirements and what happens when the technology itself changes the way people interact with digital experiences? Deque Systems CEO Preety Kumar and P&G Company Accessibility Leader Sam Latif explore the intersection of AI, regulation and digital accessibility, sharing perspectives on the challenges companies face today and the opportunities to build more accessible digital experiences.

title: Stop prompting, start directing: AI as a creative production system
description: Creative teams have never lacked ideas; they’ve lacked the means to produce them at scale. Luma COO Caroline Ingeborn explores how AI is reshaping creative production, from cutting concept development to redefining the creative director’s role. She’ll discuss how brands can maintain consistency and where teams should start to make the biggest impact.

title: From one billion dollar startup to the next
description: Juan Pablo Ortega helped build Rappi into one of Latin America’s defining technology companies. Now, as co-founder and CEO of Yuno, he is applying those lessons to a very different challenge: building the global financial infrastructure layer behind some of the world’s largest companies. In this fireside chat, Juan Pablo will discuss what changes when a founder gets the opportunity to build at scale for a second time. What did he learn from Rappi about international expansion, operating through hypergrowth and building in emerging markets? What did he deliberately do differently at Yuno? And how does starting again with the benefit of experience change decisions around product, capital, hiring and growth?

title: Leading the newsroom away from burnout
description: Covering everything from political turmoil to moments of everyday joy requires a resilient newsroom. In an era of relentless digital feeds, shrinking budgets and shifting standards, editors-in-chief must be uniquely qualified to lead their teams through constant change. This panel examines how leaders of the newsroom can sustain vital journalism without burning out.

title: America after the midterms: Trump, the Democrats and what comes next
description: With the dust now beginning to settle on the US midterm elections, our panel considers the results, their wider significance, asks the big question: what comes next? From the battle for Congress to the issues that shaped the vote, they examine the forces reshaping American politics and the lessons the election holds for both parties. With the 2028 presidential election already looming, what does the new political landscape mean for the future of Trumpism, the Democrats and the American left?

title: Spotting durable tech in an era of bubble valuations
description: In an era defined by rapid hype cycles and inflated valuations - from early crypto crazes to the AI gold rush - the line between market momentum and true enterprise value has never been blurrier. Join this session as we explore how investors look past inflated multiples to identify companies built for long-term endurance.

title: Regulating big tech
description: In a world where a handful of technology companies control the data, manage the platforms and dominate the markets that shape society, regulators face a balancing act between ensuring public safety and not jeopardising innovation or free expression. We hear from two regulators from a data protection and antitrust perspective, on how to balance these at times competing interests.

title: Why your businessʼs next loan wonʼt come from a bank
description: The traditional bank loan is facing an identity crisis. Hamstrung by outdated infrastructure and rigid criteria, legacy institutions are losing their grip on commercial credit. In their place, alternative finance platforms and algorithmic lenders are stepping in to deliver real-time liquidity. Founders and fintech leaders gather on the MoneyConf stage to unpack this shift in alternative finance and explain why business credit is moving away from traditional banks.

title: Building security for the human-machine era
description: AI has handed attackers machine speed. Defenders now have to match it without handing over the keys. Eversec founder Xiaoguang Chen makes the case for human-machine collaboration in security: machines move first, but every action is backed by evidence, authorised by people and built to withstand failure. title: Disrupting the playbook: How unlikely alliances unlock growth
description: Companies often get trapped by their own industry’s rules and miss out on gamechanging deals. Yesim founder and CEO Dmitri Verbovski and the NBA’s Milwaukee Bucks chief business development officer Matt Pazaras break down how cross-industry collaborations can spark the next wave of growth by blending rapid tech experimentation with expertise in brand and community, helping companies spot new opportunities.

title: When AI leaves the screen
description: AI transformed the digital world, now it is moving into the physical one. Robots are beginning to learn, adapt and perform new tasks in the real world without being programmed for every situation. Abhinav Gupta, Co-Founder and President of Skild AI, explores the rise of Physical AI, why one general-purpose brain could power many different robots, and what it will take to bring intelligent machines into our factories, workplaces and everyday lives.

title: The great wealth divide: “Own assets or be left behind?"
description: The Kobeissi Letter's phrase “Own assets or be left behind” describes a growing divide driven by persistent inflation, stagnating incomes for many and the emergence of a K-shaped economy. That divide has become even more pronounced amid the AI revolution, with a further widening of the gap between those who own assets and those who do not. In this talk, Adam Kobeissi explores this and the impact of AI on markets and the economy.

title: The token trap: Precision over power
description: As enterprises move from AI pilots to AI agents, per-token pricing turns every task into a metered cost, making ROI hard to predict and scale hard to justify. The answer is not bigger models. Austriacard Group AI & Data Analytics Director Spyros Sakellariou explains why precision and context deliver better results than raw model size, and how GaiaB, Austriacard's sovereign generative AI in a box, runs agentic AI on-premises at zero token cost, keeping data, IP and costs under the enterprise's control.

title: How to break your AI phone agent before your customers [Hosted by Twilio]
description: Demos look great, but real calls get messy. Join Coval and Twilio to see how smart teams test thousands of calls before going live-ensuring your AI stays sharp to power growth at scale. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: Read, render, reason: Grounding AI agents in the world [Hosted by TomTom]
description: Five lessons for grounding AI agents in the real world, from token budgets to cited answers. Live demos, a case to solve together and a first look at our new products. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: 🏅 Athletes & performance analytics meetup
description: Calling all athletes and performance analysts at Web Summit: your people are here! 🙌🏼.Exchange insights, discuss challenges, and expand your network. Join us!

title: The product strategy paradox: When technology moves faster than the roadmap
description: Product leaders are expected to build for the long term, but technology rarely stands still long enough for the plan to stay unchanged. New capabilities, startups and shifts in customer expectations can create opportunities – and force difficult decisions about where to invest, what to adapt and what to leave behind. Silicon Foundry Head of Europe Eli Promisel and Awin VP of Product Stephen Short discuss how to recognise when a new technology is worth changing the roadmap for.

title: Whose AI is it anyway? The politics underlying LLM responses
description: As AI becomes a gateway to information and truth, the values embedded within LLMs become a political issue. Do AI systems developed in the US, China and Europe answer the same questions differently, and if so what are the implications? This live field experiment explores this issue. Our panel will put questions to a range of LLMs, examine the resulting responses and assess how politics, regulation and culture have shaped these different responses.

title: The death of feature moat
description: If your competitive advantage is a thin UI wrapper on someone else's foundation model, you don't have a moat, you have a countdown timer. When any rival can clone your entire product roadmap over a weekend, features stop being differentiators. Join Granola's Sam Stephenson and Ragged Edge's Max Ottignon as they expose the engineering-first delusion, revealing why radical brand identity, opinionated craft, and taste are the only defensible moats that survive in the AI era.

title: The human bandwidth: Redefining customer experience
description: As connectivity becomes increasingly commoditised, companies are looking for new ways to deepen customer relationships and create value beyond the core service. AI, data and personalisation are changing how businesses understand customers, anticipate their needs and deliver more relevant experiences. Verisure CMO Olivier Horps, Comarch Loyalty CEO Max Byloff and MEO Chief B2C Officer Luis Mestre explore what it takes to build deeper customer relationships at scale.

title: Live Podcast: The Most Interesting Thing in AI
description:
The Most Interesting Thing in AI examines how AI is reshaping our world. Hosted by Nicholas Thompson, each episode features a conversation with a leading thinker who offers a fresh perspective on the far-reaching ethical, economic, and social implications of this technology.
This podcast is from The Atlantic’s CEO and is produced independently of The Atlantic’s editorial staff. Some episodes have a supporting sponsor. Those episodes are clearly labeled and the sponsor is named.

title: When anyone can build software, what happens next?
description: The engineering queue used to gatekeep what got built. Now the person closest to the problem can build the solution for it: employees inside nearly two-thirds of the Fortune 500 already do. When software stops being a specialist job, that changes how companies build, staff, and ship. Fabian Hedin, Lovable's Co-founder and CTO, will talk about what this transformation already looks like inside real companies, and what it takes to keep software secure when anyone can ship it.

title: Monitoring in the age of GenAI: Beyond golden signals [Hosted by Datadog]
description: A GenAI request can return 200 OK and still hallucinate, leak PII, or overspend. Learn what to measure beyond golden signals (cost, safety, quality) and how to add each to your existing monitoring. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: Nothing routine about Replit - Automations masterclass [Hosted by Replit]
description: Here you will learn all about routines in Replit, as well as how to get the most out of your AI automations. Forget about the complexities of setting up your own org chart or managing individual agents and just ask Replit. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: Why AI skills must translate into leadership access for Women
description: Join us for a meetup hosted by our community partner, Global Women Leaders in Tech

title: Towards a UN AI treaty?
description: AI is advancing faster than governments can regulate it. The UN has begun building a framework for global AI governance, but is dialogue enough? In this conversation Mary Robinson considers whether the world needs a binding UN treaty on AI, what such a treaty could cover, and whether global rules can keep pace with a technology that knows no borders.

title: The AI agent economy
description: AI is outgrowing the chat window. We are entering the era of agentic systems: autonomous software capable of reasoning, planning, and executing complex tasks directly on your behalf. But moving from passive copilots to billions of active decision-makers requires an architectural revolution at the edge. Qualcomm’s Durga Malladi reveals the low-latency compute, edge infrastructure, and trust frameworks needed to power an autonomous agent economy across everyday devices.

title: Why banking has become an AI conversation
description: Tapping through submenus to secure credit is being replaced by natural language, photo uploads and instant AI execution. The next frontier of consumer finance is not a new app UI, it is an intelligent conversation. Discover how AI-enabled banking platforms and alternative payment networks are embedding real-time lending directly into consumer intent, creating a transparent, friction-free alternative to traditional revolving debt.

title: Can Europe win the AI chip war?
description: AI is moving into a new phase, with models reasoning, coding, searching and running increasingly long sequences of work. That shift is putting new pressure on the infrastructure beneath them, from inference chips and memory to data centres and energy. As Nvidia and a handful of US tech giants dominate the current AI hardware race, where can Europe compete, and what would it take to build a meaningful AI infrastructure industry of its own?

title: The cognitive city: Where AI acts, not just sees
description: Cities, stadiums, stores and hospitals are full of sensors but short on action. Intel Edge Computing Group VP and Health and Cities Division General Manager Renu N. Navale explores how agentic and physical AI close the loop, with real examples and a clear view of where builders can win.

title: Scaling the ocean cleanup: From data to impact [Hosted by The Ocean Cleanup]
description: Follow plastic from rivers to the ocean and see how technology, data and partnerships turn cleanup into measurable, scalable impact and how you can help. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: Moving from hype to hard ROI
description: Building an AI application may be easier than ever, but scaling a profitable, defensible enterprise AI business is harder than most founders realise. This session explores how AI is transforming enterprise workflows, why energy grid and infrastructure constraints could be AI's biggest bottleneck, and what key metrics investors now demand before cutting a cheque.

timeslot_participations.job_title: General Partner & Global Head of Energy

title: The case for play
description: What if play is not the opposite of serious work, but one of our most powerful tools for solving serious problems? IDEO Partner and Managing Director Michelle Lee explores how play can unlock creativity, challenge assumptions and help people navigate complexity, from product design and workplace culture to the age of AI.

title: Orchestrated AI: From insight to iconic creative [Hosted by TransPerfect]
description: Fragmented AI tools stall enterprise marketing. See how TransPerfect’s AURA orchestrates raw data into insight, ready-to-run assets and, with The Mill, a full creative campaign. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

timeslot_participations.job_title: Senior Director Digital Strategy & Business Solutions

title: The next digital frontier
description: What will the next generation of digital economies look like? Leaders from Madeira and Pakistan share their experiences of building technology ecosystems, attracting investment and harnessing AI to transform government, business and society.

title: Day 1 marketing: How CMOs are rebuilding the org
description: AI has made experimentation easy. Transformation is harder. This talk explores what happens when CMOs move beyond deploying tools and start rethinking how marketing is organized, how decisions get made and how work reaches the customer. This session asks: if you were building marketing today with AI available from day one, would you build it the same way?

title: The ultimate competitive edge: How companies can thrive through disruption
description: In a world where AI, technology, markets and geopolitics can shift faster than corporate strategies, the ability to change is becoming a competitive capability in its own right. Roland Berger CEO Stefan Schaible explores what it takes to build organisations that can continuously adapt, moving faster from insight to decision, from decision to execution and from transformation to lasting performance.

title: Investing in zero billion dollar markets
description: Every billion-dollar industry starts as a $0B market. What massive industries don't exist yet, but will by 2030? Join this session with top investors as we unpack how to spot, fund, and build the category-defining giants of tomorrow, before the crowd arrives.

title: How AI is reprogramming the physical world
description: We are entering a new era when software doesn't just analyse data; it moves, builds, and operates in the physical world. In this session, Scott and Nina discuss why physical tech is having its breakout moment, how advancements in AI are acting as a catalyst for industries historically untouched by Silicon Valley, and where the most lucrative opportunities lie over the next few years.

title: The intelligence paradox: Why greater AI power makes human expertise more valuable
description: Accumulating the most AI tools is not the race that will set companies apart. Instead, the organisations pulling ahead are those tackling the unglamorous groundwork everyone else is skipping. Successful firms select tools directly, properly train their workforce and keep human expertise at the centre of every critical judgment call. Aaron Gibson, founder and CEO of Hurree, will expose where most rollouts go wrong and reveal what the handful of companies getting this right do differently.

title: Putting human rights into artificial intelligence
description: AI companies, such as Anthropic, have begun to think about the ethical implications of their transformative technologies by embedding a human rights respecting constitution into their AI. Should this approach become an industry standard to ensure that AI models adhere to the same moral and ethical standards as humans? Or should governments impose these standards from without?

timeslot_participations.name: Paul Tighe
timeslot_participations.job_title: Secretary of the Dicastery for Culture and Education

title: The end of genius
description: The recent advances in generative AI are profoundly changing how we create text and images. But culturally, our beliefs about how creativity happens are stuck in the 18th century, shaped by a handful of German romantic thinkers. The myth of the lone genius collides with systems that suggest that everything is simply a matter of computation. This talk explores whether AI will ultimately democratize creativity, or whether it spells the very end of the idea that made it culturally so important in the first place.

title: Solving the SMB cash crunch
description: SMBs power the global economy, yet traditional finance constantly leaves them stranded without reliable cash flow. While early fintech focused on flashy consumer apps and basic payments, a massive shift is underway. Fintech’s next groundbreaking era will solve the ultimate make-or-break hurdle for small business survival: cash flow.

description: Calling all Seed and Series A founders at Web Summit: your people are here! 🙌🏼.Exchange insights, discuss challenges, and expand your network. Join us!

title: The dog that helped with my homework, instead of eating it
description: Struggling through difficult coursework used to mean searching for answers alone, but today's students have a 24/7 tutor in their pocket. Powered by StudyFetch’s virtual assistant, Sparky the dog, students are leveraging AI to master difficult subjects at scale, developing habits of AI collaboration essential for tomorrow’s workplace. StudyFetch CEO Esan Durrani breaks down insights from eight million learners, and explains how these inspired their enterprise platform, Honen—an AI system built to continuously upskill modern teams.

title: 🇯🇵 Japan meetup
description: A space for the Japanese to connect at Web Summit 👋. Meet each other, exchange ideas, and mingle with people who get where you're from. See you there.

title: 💂🇬🇧 London startup builders meetup
description: Calling all founders, startup teams and investors building in London. Meet the people behind the city's startup scene, share what you're working on and find your next hire, co-founder or investor before you head home. See you there.

title: Silicon Valley vs. Europe and the race for global dominance
description: Global markets are in flux, forcing startups and VCs alike to adapt to a new economic reality. As funding landscapes realign, where will the next generation of industry disruptors originate? This session explores the changing dynamics between European and US tech ecosystems, looking at who is best positioned to lead the next growth cycle.

title: Building AI on your own terms: From technology discovery to real-world scale
description: Much of the world's current frontier AI capability is concentrated among a relatively small number of countries and technology providers. For the rest of the world, that concentration raises an increasingly important question: how much control do nations and businesses have over their AI future? Senen Group CEO Ronnie Sheth, Inflect CEO Mike Nguyen and Barcelona Supercomputing Center Head of AI Albert Cañigueral explore what it takes to move from AI dependency to greater control, covering infrastructure, technology and real-world scaling.

title: The next billion players will not download a game
description: Games used to be products people searched for and downloaded. AI is making games easier and cheaper to create, intensifying competition for players’ attention. The advantage is no longer just making great games, but ensuring they get discovered and building lasting relationships with players. Bozena Rezab, CEO and Co-founder of GAMEE, and David Brevik, President of Skystone Games, explore what happens to the gaming industry when anyone can make a game.

title: Building the product isn’t the hard part. Building the company is.
description: When it comes to scaling climate tech, building great energy intelligence software is only the beginning. Drawing on his experience growing Watt Footprint from a startup into a global business, Paul Mahon explores what it takes to build the company behind the technology – from bringing together the right team and securing significant funding to shaping a strong culture and scaling sustainably.

title: Why AI agents stall at the production line
description: Open standards are missing in action, causing custom AI agents to fail when scaling. Join the Linux Foundation's Mazin Gilbert as breaks down how open-source protocols eliminate proprietary lock-in and bridge the gap between impressive lab demos and reliable enterprise execution.

title: Open vs closed: The debate defining the AI era
description: As AI becomes a defining technology of the 21st century, a fundamental divide exists in how it is developed, shared and controlled. Broadly speaking, actors in China and the West are pursuing different strategies: open source collaboration vs proprietary models. This talk explores the strategic, economic, and political drivers behind openness versus control, including national security concerns, innovation incentives, and global competitiveness.

title: The playbook for brand longevity
description: Some brands survive trends. Others survive entire eras of technological change. Join this session as leaders from two iconic companies discuss how to build trust, evolve without losing your identity, and create a brand that stands the test of time.

title: Building profitable neobanks at scale
description: The initial era of neobanking was defined by rapid customer acquisition, venture-backed subsidization, and low-friction digital UX. Today, the macro environment demands a fundamental pivot toward unit economics, revenue diversification, and sustainable profitability. This panel brings together fintech founders, banking executives, and venture investors to dissect how leading digital banks are moving past hyper-growth vanity metrics to build long-term, scaleable profitability.

title: Game developers: Your next key hire
description: As AI reshapes skill requirements across industries, the games industry offers a growing pool of adaptable systems thinkers and creative problem solvers. With audience attention at a premium, are game developers the key to unlocking the next level of user engagement?

title: Reporting at the speed of news
description: Today, reporting needs to keep pace with the movement of misinformation and falsehoods on social media. How do mainstream media outlets balance the demand for instant news without jeopardising editorial integrity? Join this panel of editorial leaders as they pull back the curtain on the high-stakes balancing act of maintaining absolute accuracy under absolute pressure.

title: Taming token economics: A new framework for sustainable enterprise AI
description: Enterprises are racing to deploy generative AI and agents to lift productivity, yet face unpredictable, escalating token costs at scale. Uncontrolled token economics erodes expected efficiency gains and creates unplanned operational overhead. Explore a fresh architectural approach to balancing business value with cost predictability for large-scale AI deployment.

description: This press conference is held in the Media Village. Media event only.

timeslot_participations.job_title: EVP and GM, Technology Planning, Edge Solutions & Data Center, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.

title: What happens when AI replaces your CEO?
description: What actually happens when you replace Executive planning and decision making with AI systems built on World Models and Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI)? Join Sam Pasupalak, Co-founder & CEO of Skyfall AI, as he explores building the next frontier of AI that can continuously learn and operate SaaS businesses autonomously like an “AI CEO”, and what this entails for the future of humanity.

title: Where venture value goes next
description: Foundation models were just the starting line. Drawing on Crunchbase's proprietary data across thousands of startups, Jager McConnell reveals where the next generation of venture value is actually being built. In this session, we'll discover why tomorrow's sustainable winners are abandoning shallow wrappers to build deep moats around unique data, specialised workflows, and defensible vertical expertise.

title: Building the next generation of humans [Hosted by Life With Artificials]
description:
AI, Robotics and Synthetic biology are enabling light speed developments in human enhancements. Join us in imagining what could future humans look like and do!
Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: Don’t feed sh*t to agents
description: Operating across 50+ global markets, LUSH built “The Vault” to turn fragmented product data into a single, governed source of truth. AI agents are only as good as their context. Feed an AI agent raw, unmodeled data and it fails. LUSH CTO Simon Ince and Directus co-founder & CTO Rijk van Zanten reveal how they engineered a governed data layer that gives both humans and AI the trusted context needed to build at scale.

title: Who gets to design the future?
description: Mai Thi Nguyen, Director of the Design Lab at UC San Diego, explores how AI, design and civic technology can reshape the way cities work for the people who live in them. From housing and climate resilience to community engagement and public decision-making, she looks at how designers, technologists and communities can work together to build more inclusive, responsive and human-centred cities.

title: ✈️ Traveltech meetup
description: What's the next big shift in Traveltech? Debate it with peers who are living it 🚀. Connect with peers shaping the future of your field. Looking forward to seeing you!

title: The AI productivity paradox: Why so much AI is producing so little?
description: Trillions are being invested in AI, yet many organizations are still struggling to translate adoption into meaningful productivity gains. The problem may not be the models, but the way companies are deploying them. CNTR CEO and Aleph Alpha co-founder Jonas Andrulis examines what needs to change for AI to become embedded in how organizations actually make decisions, solve problems and create value.

title: From copilot to colleague: How AI agents join your team
description: Every team has an AI copilot, but few have an AI colleague. The difference? Colleagues know the context, own their work and get better every week without being asked twice. Drawing on lessons from building Strawberry Browser and helping teams put agents to work, Charles Maddock shares what it takes to bring agents onto the team and how leaders can build an AI-native team starting Monday.

title: China’s global brand revolution
description: Chinese brands are making a bigger mark on markets around the world, from consumer technology and automotive to fashion and beauty. This keynote looks at the brands that have cracked the global market and the creative strategies behind their success, offering lessons that any brand can take from a new generation of global challengers.

title: Should we build AGI?
description: As trillions flow into the race for monolithic Artificial General Intelligence, a pragmatic question emerges: Is AGI actually the most economically viable architecture for productive enterprise work? In this debate, Cognizant Chief AI Officer Babak Hodjat makes the case for lean networks of composable, domain-specific agents—challenging frontier model leaders on whether general intelligence is a costly distraction from scalable, specialized AI.

title: The Portuguese economic success story
description: Portugal's economy has, despite unfavourable international headwinds, maintained strong growth. GDP per capita has increased for at least 4 straight years, unemployment is at an over 10-year low, and government debt continues to fall. We will hear from the Minister of Finance in charge of many of the reforms that have spurred this positive performance about how Portugal has gone from strength to strength.

timeslot_participations.name: Joaquim Miranda Sarmento
timeslot_participations.job_title: Minister of State and of Finance

title: The perks of loyalty: How embedded rewards turn everyday spending into revenue
description: Loyalty has shifted from a cost centre to a core revenue driver, where integration speed matters far more than reward size. Drawing on more than 30 white-label implementations across Europe, Finperks co-founder and CEO Sebastian Seifert explores why one embedded product fits three different industries – banks, fintechs and HR SaaS platforms. Discover what actually gets business cases signed, why implementation speed beats price in closing deals and how to compress launch timelines from months to weeks.

title: The race for compute, agentic AI, and ROI
description: Join Philippe Botteri as he unveils key findings from Accel's annual Globalscape report. Moving beyond software into a massive infrastructure buildout, this session explores where VC billions are flowing, from agentic systems and compute battles to open vs. closed source models, and reveals where real ROI is materialising across the global ecosystem.

title: What happens when machines start asking questions at scale?
description: Working with AI agents on data analytics is quickly becoming the standard for data analysts and decision makers. But is the data infrastructure underneath optimized for this new reality? In the age of agents, the way we analyze data is fundamentally changing. Mark Kardashov, CEO and Co-Founder of Keewano, explores what this shift means for data infrastructure and data modeling, and whether today’s data stack is ready for what comes next.

title: Making sense of the promise and hype of the AI agent economy
description: AI has overinvested in producing intelligence and underinvested in determining where that intelligence deserves capital. This talk looks beyond the buzzwords to explore where AI agents are creating real economic value today, where they are not, and what it will take to turn increasingly capable AI into meaningful, scalable businesses especially as we approach what some describe as an “agentic singularity.”

title: When AI verifies AI
description: Traditional software follows strict rules: input A always equals output B. AI is different – it improvises, adapts, and sometimes makes things up. When an app never gives the exact same answer twice, how do you guarantee it stays accurate and safe? Join TestMu AI's Asad Khan as he breaks down how teams use smart AI testing tools to catch hallucinated facts, stress-test security, and keep customer-facing AI on the rails.

title: The biggest buyout in history was a games company
description: EA has just gone private in a $55bn deal, the largest LBO ever. It marks a defining moment for gaming: its biggest franchises are no longer just cultural phenomena, but some of the world’s most valuable creative properties. This panel brings together the people financing game IP, the founders who built and sold it, and the operators running studios through change. What are people really buying when a game world changes hands? Can financial backing coexist with creative ambition, player trust and long-term investment?

title: In bots we trust: Defending money against AI-powered fraud
description: AI has made fraud cheaper, faster and easier to scale: deepfakes beat voice and video checks, synthetic identities slip through onboarding, and instant payments leave no time to react. This fireside chat explores what works now: custom AI models tuned to a company’s own users, and layered identity defences combining AI, behavioural and device signals, and human review, that stop evolving attacks without adding friction. And as AI agents start moving money for us, how do we keep trust intact?

title: Less is more: AI's next race is efficiency
description: The first AI cycle was defined by scale: bigger models, more compute, and unprecedented infrastructure. The next cycle will increasingly be defined by who can make AI more efficient and accessible across the stack. Rocio Wu of F-Prime breaks down the AI stack from the ground up, from energy grids and cooling systems to chip design and smart software, to show where the biggest bottlenecks are today. As the industry opens up and becomes more competitive, the next major winners will be those who can deliver smart results with fewer resources.

title: Trust me bro: Western media and the decline of public trust
description: Public trust in mainstream media has fallen sharply across much of the West, as audiences question everything from editorial independence to the influence of governments, corporations and powerful interests. This talk explores whether this crisis of confidence is the result of misinformation, political polarisation, and social media? Or whether traditional journalism has lost credibility on its own terms?

title: Who do you trust when no one's human?
description: Trust used to come from a name you recognised. Now it’s built through every interaction, from instant payments to deliveries that arrive as promised. Wolff Olins CEO Sairah Ashman explores how technology has changed what we trust, and why brands must prove their values in every moment. Drawing on Wolff Olins’ work reimagining legacy brands and creating new ones, she’ll explore what it takes to earn trust in a world where your product is your brand.

description: Calling all founders, startup teams and investors building in Paris. Meet the people behind the city's startup scene, share what you're working on and find your next hire, co-founder or investor before you head home. See you there.

title: The next financial crisis: Are we ready for what's coming?
description: With record public and private debt, geopolitical fragmentation and AI-driven market shifts, are the conditions for another financial crisis already in place? This talk examines the biggest risks facing the global financial system, from sovereign debt and central bank policy to asset bubbles, private credit, and geopolitical shocks. Our panel will debate whether today's economy is fundamentally more resilient than in 2008, or whether we're simply waiting for the next trigger.

title: The new battleground in the AI race
description: The battle for AI supremacy has shifted from training to runtime execution. As models evolve into reasoning engines and autonomous agents, latency is the hard ceiling on what developers can build. Join Cerebras Systems Chief Strategy Officer Andy Hock to explore how ultra-fast inference is powering the next generation of AI applications.

title: Human moat in the machine era
description: As artificial intelligence becomes ubiquitous, raw compute and software generation are rapidly commoditized. The ultimate commercial moat is no longer the algorithm; it's human judgment, leadership, and execution speed. Join Idealab's Bill Gross and Lattice's Sarah Franklin discuss why emotional intelligence, cultural alignment, and human grit become dramatically more valuable as AI scales across the economy.

title: How do you build creative ambition?
description: Creativity can be trained. But how do you unlock it in others? Luiza Baffa, Head of Creative Studio at On, in conversation with Jean Rosier, Partner & CCO of Perestroika, explore how we build creative confidence and ambition, from developing our own creative muscles to creating environments where people feel empowered to experiment, take risks and do their best work.

title: The new financing frontier: How intellectual property unlocks capital
description: Turning ideas into growth at scale remains a challenge for startups and businesses across Europe. How can IP-backed finance unlock a new source of capital? Business Angels Slovenia President Nina Dremelj and European Union Intellectual Property Office Deputy Executive Director Andrea Di Carlo explore the opportunity, the barriers to scaling IP-backed finance and the market and regulatory changes needed to turn Europe’s intellectual property into investable capital.

title: Your AI doesn't know your market, and here's how to fix that
description: When enterprises today ask AI for market strategy, web-trained models yield the same generic answers. To unlock precise, high-stakes decisions, Rwazi’s Kapil Mathrani introduces a three-layer approach combining internal company data, macro-market trends and first-party behavioural data shared voluntarily by five million consumers. Discover how combining these layers delivers precise insights and why transparent data collection is key to outputs you can actually trust.

title: Who pays for infinite output?
description: When machines can generate without limit, the constraint moves entirely onto the people deciding, approving and absorbing what gets made. This session explores AI, existentialism and the human cost of running an organization at a pace no human timeline was built for.

title: Sourcing, signals and the future of deal flow
description: How do you find the next $100B startup when everyone is looking in the same places? From corporate intelligence networks and global pitch engines to algorithmic deal flow, top VCs are rewriting their sourcing playbooks. In this session, we discuss how leading investors cut through market noise and back tomorrow's category leaders before the rest of the market catches on.

title: Building the genAI-native banking tools
description: While most banks use AI for basic customer support, bunq is rebuilding core financial experiences around generative models. Join CSO Bianca Zwart to learn how Europe’s second-largest neobank uses native GenAI to eliminate financial admin friction and deliver truly autonomous banking.

title: From space missions to space infrastructure
description: The space industry is shifting from individual missions and bespoke systems towards scalable, interconnected infrastructure. Yet unlocking its full potential requires overcoming two fundamental challenges: scale and interoperability. This talk explains how the transition towards shared, service-oriented infrastructure can make space more accessible and commercially relevant. Drawing on SpaceComputer's approach to bridging terrestrial and orbital computing, explore how services such as key management and secure computing can become building blocks for space-enabled applications.

title: Beyond the bans: Protecting Youth Rights in a fragmented online world
description: Across Europe and beyond, governments are racing to regulate childrens' access to the internet with age verification mandates, platform bans, screen-time restrictions, and different sets of national rules that rarely align with one another. But as the policy landscape fragments, the question must be asked: how can governments and privacy agencies better align to ensure the safety of kids and prevent the access to problematic content being confined to the darker corners of the internet.

description: As AI and algorithms increasingly shape how people navigate the world, genuine human connection has never been more sought after or more valuable. Reddit COO Jen Wong explores why the next era of the internet will depend not on more information, but on trusted context, personal opinion and firsthand experience, considering how authentic human dialogue can strengthen AI, search & discovery while keeping people at the centre of an increasingly automated internet.

title: Here comes the sun: Why we need an energy system in space
description: The energy transition is not only a generation challenge – it is a delivery challenge. As demand accelerates, grids, geography and intermittency are becoming the binding constraints on getting reliable power where and when it is needed. Harvesting solar energy in space and beaming it to Earth separates where energy is produced from where it is consumed, changing the geography of energy itself. This talk explores how space-based energy complements the terrestrial system, strengthens European energy sovereignty and moves us from managing scarcity toward building abundance.

title: Teaching AI to see the world
description: AI has learned to describe the world in words. The next frontier is teaching AI to understand the world as it really is: made of objects, movement, space, sound, and cause and effect. Visual intelligence gives machines a richer understanding of that reality. In this keynote, Andi Blattmann explores how Black Forest Labs is building the foundation of this next layer of intelligence, and how this foundation enables the next generation of physical AI.

title: EU enlargement: is bigger actually better?
description: The EU is preparing for its biggest potential expansion in decades, as Ukraine, the Western Balkans and other candidate countries seek membership. Enlargement could strengthen Europe’s geopolitical influence and bring greater stability to its neighbourhood. Yet it could also make decision-making, funding and political cohesion much harder. This talk asks whether bigger really does mean better, and can unity and effectiveness be maintained in an increasingly uncertain world?

title: What jobs no longer require humans?

He answers the question with anonymised data instead of predictions: which jobs companies have actually handed over, which ones companies tried and failed to automate and which he expects to go next.

title: Craft at scale: what AI means for the future of design
description: AI is changing how creative work gets made, from the tools designers reach for to the skills that separate good work from great work. Duncan Clark, Managing Director EMEA and CEO of Pro Design at Canva, looks at what happens when craft meets scale: how workflows are shifting, what stays uniquely human in the process, and what it means to be a designer when creative tools are in everyone's hands. It's a look at where the industry is heading, and what that means for the people who've spent their careers mastering the craft.

description: Much of the world has stood by and watched the Palestinian people be decimated by war, famine, and destruction. Not all have ignored their plight, however. In this talk Tech for Palestine founder Paul Biggar will talk through what the tech sector is doing to help, and how much more needs to be done.

title: The best offense is a machine-speed defence
description: As AI reshapes technology, one truth holds: innovation can only move as fast as the security protecting it. The same AI empowering defenders is supercharging attackers at machine speed. CrowdStrike CEO and Founder George Kurtz explores why security is the foundation of the AI era, letting business move faster and safer. From cloud networks to split-second Formula 1 data, see why the companies that win with AI are the ones that secure it first.

title: The new rules of audience development
description: The strongest media businesses understand that audience development and business development are deeply connected. This talk examines how data, editorial insight, community building, and experimentation can help media organisations understand who their audiences are, and more importantly, what those audiences need. It explores how deeper audience relationships can drive loyalty, growth, and new commercial opportunities.

title: Everyone wants autonomous AI. Nobody wants to give up control.
description: While 75 percent of global employees use AI daily, a critical confidence gap remains between what AI can technically automate and what leaders trust autonomous agents to execute. With IT leaders projecting that nearly 40 percent of workplace services will run autonomously by 2030, concerns over visibility, governance and control threaten to stall progress. In this session, TeamViewer CEO Oliver Steil, Otter.ai CEO Sam Liang and RemoFirst CEO Nurasyl Serik examine how enterprise research, real-time communication AI and cross-border workforce compliance intersect to solve this trust deficit – showing that long-term success relies not on deploying the most AI tools, but on building the guardrails and human oversight needed to move safely from simple assistance to trusted autonomy.

title: Hormones as the next frontier of women’s longevity and healthspan
description: Women spend 25 percent more of their lives in poor health than men, yet the industry directs only one percent of healthcare research towards female-specific conditions beyond oncology. At 22, Jenny turned this healthcare blindspot into Clair Health, building the first noninvasive continuous hormone-monitoring wearable. In this Growth Summit keynote, Jenny shares how continuous data helps women understand their bodies, and how the company built scientific rigour and consumer trust to raise US$11.6 million.

title: AI's next billion-dollar market
description: As foundation models proliferate and specialise, the battle for AI value capture is shifting. Is the next billion-dollar market created at the application layer, or down in the developer infrastructure and security pipelines? Join this session as we debate the state of the multi-modal stack, where the defensible moats are being built, and where VCs are placing their biggest bets.

title: Normal is not safe
description: As intelligence gets cheaper and sameness gets easier, competitive advantage moves to the edges: unusual thinkers, pattern-breakers and people who see what everyone else misses. Kim Lawrie, Head of Innovation at ustwo, discusses the case for neurodivergent talent as a competitive advantage and asks: what if the greatest risk in business is no longer being wrong, but becoming indistinguishable?

title: Scaling what cannot be standardized
description: Industrial software is difficult to scale because every company operates under different constraints, meaning companies cannot easily standardise their operations. ALGO ARTIS grew by identifying the common structures beneath complex problems and turning each deployment into reusable technology, software and industry knowledge. Kentaro shares why this alone is not enough – and how scaling across energy, manufacturing, and logistics also requires different approaches to customisation, pricing and product strategy for each market.

title: What happens if open source wins?
description: This talk explores the growing divide between open and closed AI from the promise of openness, transparency and wider access, to the case for proprietary models, greater control and responsible deployment. But what happens if open-source AI wins? As increasingly powerful models become freely available, could widespread access accelerate innovation and competition or create systemic risks that extend far beyond the technology sector? What could the rapid proliferation of powerful open models mean for financial markets, institutions and the stability of the global financial system? What does “open” really mean when it comes to AI, and where should the line be drawn between openness and control? Does open AI democratise access and drive innovation, or does it make powerful capabilities harder to govern and contain? And as the technology evolves, will the future of AI be truly open or closed or something in between?

title: The enterprise reality check
description: As AI systems become more powerful and technology ecosystems more interconnected, enterprises are being forced to confront a difficult reality: can they explain, govern, and regain control of the technology their business depends on? IBM will debut exclusive research exploring the gap between confidence and capability, uncovering what failure could cost, where organisations are most vulnerable, and what separates true leaders from those whose control was never as strong as they believed.

Founders building the infrastructure and policymakers writing the rules go head to head on whether tokenisation is genuine reform or Wall Street's old model with a new coat of paint.

This panel explores how marketers are adapting as the places where people discover products, make decisions and transact increasingly overlap, and what brands need to do to stay relevant and trusted along the way.

title: What Europe can learn from China: From industrial strategy to tech
description: China’s rise as an industrial and technological powerhouse raises an important question for Europe: what can we learn from its approach? From EVs, batteries and solar power to high-speed rail and robotics, China has achieved remarkable scale and speed. This talk explores what Europe can learn from China’s industrial strategy, investment and approach to technological competitiveness.

title: Is AI flattening the tech market or concentrating it?
description: The lopsided market conditions have kept everyone wondering for some time now; is there a bubble, and what happens next? Simply ‘investing in AI’ is not a sustainable strategy. Mattias Ljungman of Moonfire Ventures offers a concrete view of what constitutes long-term value when nothing seems certain.

title: The instant economy: Why are we still waiting for our own money?
description: Despite real-time rails and instant settlement capabilities, everyday finance remains bound by legacy schedules. This discussion examines the shift to instant payments, earned wage access, and how real-time money movement impacts risk, regulation, and consumer flexibility.

title: Capital beyond equity
description: Europe’s emerging AI hardware, robotics and industrial automation sectors require massive upfront capex, yet traditional venture capital is ill-equipped to fund physical infrastructure and risk-averse commercial banks refuse to extend debt to unproven technology models. Burning dilutive equity to build factories or buy machinery is a structural mistake that bleeds founder control and stalls scale. Bringing together deep tech investors, robotics founders and debt infrastructure pioneers, this session explores the financial mechanics needed to fund Europe’s reindustrialisation, from asset-backed securitisation to performance-guaranteed equipment debt, without surrendering founder equity.

title: Building new worlds: Before AI there was imagination
description: Before AI, worlds were built by hand. David Jones and David Brevik built some of gaming's biggest – Grand Theft Auto, Diablo – and watched them grow into billion-dollar assets, traded long after the imagining was done. How do you build a world people never leave, and what is it ultimately worth?

title: The worlds where AI learns to act
description: Most AI models learn from human-generated data, but machines that will drive vehicles, operate equipment and move through physical space need something different: a working understanding of how the world behaves. Odyssey co-founder and CEO Oliver Cameron argues that training models on reality enables them to adapt quickly to new hardware with minimal fine-tuning. Crucially, these models can also simulate realistic environments to test actions and uncover safety risks before they reach the physical world.

title: Betting on people: Building the opportunity economy
description: The next era of the creator economy will be defined by the companies willing to invest in the people behind the work. Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, explores the power of backing individuals, supporting artists and creating real opportunities for creators to thrive. From putting photographers at the centre of its community to supporting them in the physical world, he explores how investing in people can build a creator economy that works for both creators and the businesses behind them.

timeslot_participations.name: Kate Lindsay
timeslot_participations.job_title: Writer, Embedded and host of Slate's ICYMI podcast

title: Where code meets crater
description: Operating AI on the Moon means navigating uncharted terrain without GPS, strict power limits, or direct control from Earth. Explore what it takes to build autonomous robotic workforces for deep space. Balancing machine intelligence, human oversight, and the harsh realities of extreme environments. Warning: May contain an actual lunar rover on stage.

title: The path to processing US$10bn in payments
description: Compliance cannot be a bottleneck if you want to scale, and regulation has to be approached as a partnership, not an obstacle. Bernardo shares how building local banking relationships market by market, rather than trying to route around them, turned Trace Finance into core infrastructure for four of the world's largest payment providers operating in LatAm.

title: Coaching an AI agent like human talent
description: Deploying enterprise voice AI isn't a set-and-forget software install; like the rest of your business, it has to adapt to evolving business logic and customer expectations. Join Nikola Mrkšić, Co-Founder and CEO of PolyAI, to hear how enterprise leaders are using AI agents behind-the-scenes to constantly coach and improve the AI agents that actually speak with their customers, and where human decision-making is still critical.

description: Understand. Reimagine. Prioritise. Learn how to rapidly analyse business processes, uncover hidden inefficiencies, identify where AI creates real value, and build a transformation roadmap grounded in business outcomes, economics, and operational impact.
